title.narrative: Strategic Purchasing and Alignment of Resources & Knowledge in Health Project (SPARK-Health)

description.narrative: The development objective of the Strategic Purchasing and Alignment of Resources and Knowledge in Health Project for Cote d'Ivoire is to improve the utilization and quality of health services towards reducing maternal and infant mortality in the Recipient's territory. The project comprises of four components. The first component, scale-up of strategic purchasing consists of following sub-components: (i) extension of performance-based financing (PBF) in the context of strategic purchasing; (ii) scale-up of national health insurance (CMU); and (iii) support for health reforms and national capacity building. The second component, health system strengthening to improve performance consists of following sub-components: (i) rehabilitation, equipment, and environmental sanitation; (ii) reproductive health and nutrition; (iii) strengthening health human resources; and (iv) governance and health management information systems (HMIS). The third component, project management consists of following sub-components: (i) project coordination; (ii) monitoring-evaluation (monitoring, supervision, and support); and (iii) knowledge sharing and dissemination of results. The fourth component, contingent emergency response component (CERC) will allow for rapid reallocation of project proceeds in the event of a natural or man-made disaster or crisis that has caused or is likely to imminently cause a major adverse economic and or social impact.

To improve the utilization and quality of health services towards reducing maternal and infant mortality, and to provide immediate and effective response to an eligible crisis or emergency, in the Recipient's territory.

title.narrative: Health Facilities rehabilitated and / or equipped

comment.narrative: This indicator includes all health infrastructures rehabilitated or equipped under the Project, including those health facilities that were improved (rehabilitated and/or equipped) using the PBF subsidies.
This indicator's target was set as an estimate of 70 percent of the population that would benefit from this project intervention, a standard for COVID-19 projects.
This indicator was included following the midterm review of the project to reflect the number of staff within the project implementing unit who benefit from training during the project life.

This indicator reported the number of services provided, rather than the number of beneficiaries. It captures health services provided and other interventions (such as training) that benefited health and project staff. This end of project value does not include the beneficiaries covered thanks the COVID response. The targets and achievements in this indicator are higher than the total number of the population because it reflects services provided as captured by the quarterly reports. The number of direct beneficiaries was 18,618,871 of which 13,591,776 are women (73%)

title.narrative: Number of poor and vulnerable who benefit from health services using the CMU card.

comment.narrative: The wording of this indicator was revised to better capture the achievement of the PDO: increase access to and utilization of quality health services. The revised indicator measures the number of poor and vulnerable people who used their CMU card to benefit from health services in the districts targeted by the Project. While the indicator intends to measure achievements for the most vulnerable population, by completion, 52 percent of the population was enrolled in the CMU. The Project was instrumental in achieving this outcome: expanding enrollment, facilitating synergies between the PBF and the CMU, promoting and disseminating information about the CMU. The number of indigents as identified by the government was 1,200,000 people.
